description:
Build a household location choice model using the San Francisco UrbanSim data.

Task: Using Jupyter Lab and statsmodels/sklearn, estimate a logistic regression model that predicts household location choices based on building characteristics.

REQUIREMENTS:
- Open the Jupyter notebook at /home/ga/urbansim_projects/notebooks/location_choice.ipynb
- Load the San Francisco data from /home/ga/urbansim_projects/data/sanfran_public.h5
- Load both the 'households' and 'buildings' tables
- Merge households with their building information using building_id (note: building_id is the index of the buildings table, so merge using left_on='building_id' and right_index=True)
- Create a binary dependent variable for the choice model (e.g., whether a building has above-median residential_units, or any reasonable binary classification of location quality)
- Use at least 3 building features as independent variables (e.g., residential_sales_price, building_sqft, year_built)
- Fit a logistic regression model using statsmodels Logit or sklearn LogisticRegression
- Print the model summary with coefficients and significance
- Save the model coefficients to /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/location_choice_coefficients.csv with columns: variable, coefficient
- Save a bar chart of coefficient magnitudes to /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/location_choice_coefficients.png

The notebook should be executed with all cells run.
